ideas.title: Everdell Tree-Spine Card Browser & Berry Silo
ideas.concept: A stylized tree-trunk stand with 12 radiating slanted slots that let a player fan through Everdell's city/meadow cards like a rolodex during play, with a small integrated silo at the base that holds and dispenses berry/resin/pebble/twig resource tokens by color-coded chute.
ideas.rationale: Everdell is a top-50 BGG game frequently cited in 2026 cozy-game roundups (Elizabeth Hargrave-adjacent 'cozy games' coverage from GameSpot and Her Cozy Gaming's 2026 list) and has an active 3D-print insert community on MakerWorld/Printables, but virtually all existing Everdell prints are flat storage-tray inserts for the box, not in-play browsing aids.
ideas.differentiation: Confirmed via search that existing Everdell 3D prints (Printables, MakerWorld) are box-storage trays used only during setup/teardown. This is instead an active-play accessory used at the table while browsing the meadow/city, shaped as a decorative tree trunk rather than a grid tray — a distinct use-case and aesthetic niche not covered by the insert-focused listings found.
ideas.producibility_notes: 2 parts: trunk/card-fan body (single piece, no supports needed if printed slot-side up) and a separate resource silo insert that press-fits into the trunk base (friction-fit tab, tolerance 0.2mm, no glue/hardware). Two-color print recommended (bark-brown trunk, tan card slots) via color change at set layer; single-color also viable. No features under 1mm; slot walls kept at 2mm minimum.
ideas.margin_case: ~140g PLA, ~7hr print, two-part FDM. Sell at $28. A themed table accessory for a beloved cozy-game fanbase commands a premium over a plain tray insert because it's a visible, giftable centerpiece piece, not a hidden box liner.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A tabletop card-browsing stand shaped like a stylized tree trunk, roughly cylindrical and tapering slightly toward the top, with 12 angled card slots cut radially around its upper half so a fanned deck of standard 63x88mm cards can be flipped through one at a time without removing them from the stand. A separate cup-shaped resource silo (approx 50mm diameter, 40mm tall) with 4 internal color-coded vertical chutes press-fits into a matching socket in the base of the trunk. Purpose: A board-game table accessory for players of nature/engine-building board games (e.g. Everdell) to browse a market/meadow row of cards during play and dispense small wooden/resin resource tokens, sold to hobbyist board gamers as a decorative upgrade accessory. Style: Warm woodland theme — bark texture on the trunk exterior, smooth interior slot walls, organic tapering silhouette, no license artwork, natural brown/tan color palette. Technical specification: Overall trunk height 110mm, base diameter 70mm tapering to 55mm at top; 12 card slots each 3mm wide x 70mm deep angled 15 degrees outward from vertical, slot wall thickness minimum 2mm; silo component 50mm diameter x 40mm tall with a 30mm deep friction-fit tenon (0.2mm clearance) matching a socket in the trunk base, 4 internal dividers each 1.5mm thick splitting the silo into four token compartments with a single top opening per compartment approximately 15mm wide. Material: PLA, FDM printable with no supports if trunk is oriented slot-openings-up and silo printed base-down. Two-part assembly, no glue or hardware, no threads. Two-color option: bark-brown trunk body, tan/cream card slot inserts via layer color change; single-color print also acceptable.

ideas.title: Cozy Games Nesting Hex Canister Set
ideas.concept: A set of 4 lidded hexagonal canisters that nest inside one another for storage (largest holds the next size down, etc.) and unstack into a small hex-grid cluster during play to hold resource tokens, wildlife tiles, or eggs for cozy euro games.
ideas.rationale: BGG's own 'This Now is Trending' 2026 trend blog and multiple 2026 cozy-games roundups (GameSpot, Her Cozy Gaming) confirm a genuine and growing 'cozy/slow-living' board game genre (Cascadia, Wingspan, Everdell, and Hargrave's upcoming Sanibel) whose fans specifically favor soft, nature-toned aesthetics over generic black plastic organizers.
ideas.differentiation: Search of existing token-storage prints on Printables/MakerWorld/Thingiverse shows almost all are open, non-nested trays or bowls sold as single-game-specific inserts; a closed-lid, cork-look, nesting-for-travel canister set that is deliberately game-agnostic (works across the whole cozy-game shelf, not one title) and collapses to the volume of its single largest piece is not a pattern found in that search.
ideas.producibility_notes: 4 parts, each printed separately, single color per canister (offer in muted sage/cream/terracotta/tan as color options) with a snap-fit lid (press-past-a-lip, no hinge, no hardware). Wall thickness 1.6mm, lid lip tolerance 0.15mm for a firm but removable snap. No features under 1mm.
ideas.margin_case: ~180g PLA total across 4 canisters, ~9hr combined print, sell as a set for $24. Buyers of the cozy-game genre are documented gift-givers (holiday/birthday 'game night upgrade' purchases per cozy-game blog coverage), and a matched nesting set reads as a coherent accessory rather than a loose single tray, supporting a set price over a single-part price.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A set of 4 hexagonal lidded canisters of graduated sizes (largest 70mm across flats x 45mm tall, down to smallest 45mm across flats x 30mm tall) that nest fully inside one another (each canister's outer diameter clears the next size up's inner cavity with 0.3mm play) for compact storage, and separate into a cluster of 4 individual token-holding pots for use during gameplay. Each canister has a press-fit hexagonal lid with a small thumb notch for removal. Purpose: A game-agnostic token/resource storage accessory for players of nature-themed 'cozy' board games (bird, wildlife, farming, and tile-laying euro games), sold as a decorative table accessory and gift item for board-game hobbyists. Style: Soft, natural aesthetic — matte finish, muted single-color per canister chosen from sage green, cream, terracotta, and tan, cork-look ribbed texture on lid tops, no game-specific artwork or licensed branding. Technical specification: 4 hexagonal canisters with flat-to-flat widths of 70mm, 60mm, 52mm, and 45mm respectively, heights 45mm, 40mm, 35mm, 30mm respectively, wall thickness 1.6mm throughout. Each canister has a separate snap-fit lid: a shallow hexagonal cap with a 3mm deep interior lip sized 0.15mm smaller than the canister's inner opening for a firm friction-fit snap, plus a 10mm x 4mm thumb notch cut into the lid rim for easy removal. Nesting requirement: each canister's outer wall must clear the next-larger canister's inner cavity by 0.3mm so all 4 stack fully inside the largest one with lids removed. Material: PLA, FDM, single color per part, no supports required if printed lid-up/canister-base-down, no glue or hardware, 4 separate printed parts with no assembly beyond lid press-fit.

ideas.title: Print-in-Place Zero-Hardware Dice Vault
ideas.concept: A single continuous print-in-place dice tray/tower/storage box that folds flat for storage and pops open into a full dice tower with catch tray using only built-in living hinges — no magnets, no glue, no separate parts to lose.
ideas.rationale: Search confirms folding/magnetic dice towers are one of the most common categories on Thingiverse/Printables/MyMiniFactory (dozens of active listings), meaning there is durable, proven buyer demand for this object class in the tabletop hobby, independent of any single title.
ideas.differentiation: Every existing design found (Patrick Latcham's Magnetic Dice Box/Tray/Tower, heyItsDubbleA's Magnetic Dice Tower, Filament_3d_Printing's foldable tray) requires the end user to source and glue 4-8 loose magnets after printing. This design is deliberately specified as a single print-in-place part with integrated hinges and a friction-latch closure, so it ships fully assembled and ready to use with zero post-print hardware or assembly — a meaningful advantage specifically for buyers who don't own a workshop or spare magnets, i.e. exactly this platform's customer.
ideas.producibility_notes: 1 part, print-in-place with 4 built-in living hinges (0.6mm hinge thickness, printed flat on the bed so no supports are needed inside the folding mechanism). Single color. Requires a printer capable of clean small-clearance print-in-place joints (0.3mm hinge-pin clearance) — flagged as a moderate-risk feature to validate in a test print before full production run.
ideas.margin_case: ~110g PLA, ~6hr print, sell at $22. Zero-assembly convenience justifies a price above bare-bones tray designs (which sell for $10-15 pre-assembled on Etsy) because the buyer is paying to skip magnet-sourcing and gluing entirely.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A single print-in-place folding dice tower and catch-tray combo. In its closed/flat state it is a compact rectangular slab; unfolding along 4 built-in living hinges reveals a zig-zag interior ramp (dice tower) that stands upright and empties into an attached shallow catch tray, held open by a simple friction tab-and-slot latch (no magnets). Purpose: A portable dice-rolling accessory for tabletop board and RPG gamers who want a compact, assembly-free dice tower for home or travel use, sold pre-printed and ready to use out of the box. Style: Minimal/utilitarian geometric design, single flat color, subtle faceted low-poly surface texturing for grip and visual interest, no game-specific branding. Technical specification: Folded/flat footprint approximately 100mm x 70mm x 15mm; unfolded standing height approximately 140mm with a catch tray footprint of 100mm x 70mm. One single printed part using 4 built-in living hinges each 0.6mm thick x 40mm wide, printed flat/closed on the print bed so the hinges form with no supports required inside the fold lines. Internal zig-zag ramp consists of 3 baffles spaced to slow falling dice, minimum ramp wall thickness 2mm. Closure/latch: a 4mm x 8mm friction tab molded into the tower's top panel that presses into a matching slot on the tray panel to hold the tower upright during play, tolerance 0.2mm for a firm push-fit without cracking the hinge. Material: PLA, single color, no glue, no magnets, no metal hardware, one part, zero post-print assembly required beyond first-time unfolding.

ideas.title: Woodland Critter Sculpted Meeple Upgrade Set
ideas.concept: A set of 6 sculpted animal-silhouette standee pieces (fox, owl, hedgehog, rabbit, badger, deer), each on a round base, sized as a drop-in worker-placement piece upgrade for any euro-style board game that ships with plain wooden meeples or cubes.
ideas.rationale: Cross-game 'meeple upgrade' sets are an established Etsy/Printables purchase category for board-game hobbyists customizing games like Wingspan, Everdell, and Cascadia, and the 2026 cozy/nature-game genre trend (BGG trend blog, GameSpot cozy-games coverage) specifically favors woodland-animal aesthetics over generic pawns.
ideas.differentiation: Search of existing custom-meeple listings shows most are either single flat pawn shapes with printed decals, or a single 'generic animeeple' blob shared across species; this set instead gives each of the 6 species a distinct sculpted side-profile silhouette (visibly different outline per animal, not just a color/decal change) and is explicitly sold as a universal cross-game upgrade rather than tied to one licensed title.
ideas.producibility_notes: 6 small parts (one per animal), each roughly 22mm tall, printed on a shared base plate in a single batch. Two-color option (body + base) via swap, single-color also viable. No overhangs beyond 45 degrees to keep supports minimal; ear/tail details kept at or above 1.2mm to stay within reliable FDM tolerance.
ideas.margin_case: ~35g PLA total for the 6-piece set, ~3hr print, sell at $18. Gift-buyers for board-game hobbyists routinely pay $15-25 for cosmetic upgrade sets on Etsy; a 6-species set with distinct sculpting (vs. one repeated shape) supports the higher end of that range.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A set of 6 individual miniature standee figures, each a distinct woodland animal silhouette (fox, owl, hedgehog, rabbit, badger, deer) standing on a round base, sized to match standard board-game worker-placement pieces. Each figure is a simplified, low-detail sculptural side-profile (not a full 3D-in-the-round sculpt) so it reads clearly as its species from any viewing angle while remaining robust for handling. Purpose: A cosmetic upgrade/replacement piece set for board-game hobbyists who want to replace generic wooden meeples or cubes in nature-themed euro games (e.g. bird, farming, or wildlife-themed titles) with characterful animal pieces; sold as a gift item and collector accessory. Style: Simplified modern-folk-art sculptural silhouette, smooth rounded forms, no fine fur texture, single flat color per figure (offer natural earth-tone palette: fox in rust orange, owl in slate gray, hedgehog in brown, rabbit in cream, badger in charcoal/white, deer in tan) or optional single uniform color for the whole set. Technical specification: Each figure approximately 20-24mm tall x 12-15mm wide, standing on a circular base 16mm diameter x 3mm thick. All 6 figures share one base thickness and diameter so they are interchangeable with standard meeple footprints. Minimum feature thickness 1.2mm on ears, tails, and other thin protrusions to remain printable without breaking. Orient each figure so overhangs stay under 45 degrees from vertical to minimize support material; if supports are required, restrict them to the base plate only, not the figure body. Material: PLA or PETG, FDM, 6 separate small parts printable together in one batch on a shared build plate, no assembly, no hardware, single color per part (optional 2-color body/base split via manual filament swap).

ideas.title: Box-Edge Clip-On Score Dial
ideas.concept: A rotating score-tracking dial (0-50, two full turns to 100) that clips onto the rim/edge of any standard board-game box lid via a flexible spring-jaw clip, so the tracker stays physically attached to the game's own box between sessions instead of rattling loose inside.
ideas.rationale: Universal score-track dials and clip-style accessories are an established, repeatedly-listed category on Etsy and Printables aimed at board-game households who play many different titles and want one reusable scoring tool rather than a per-game insert; this is a durable cross-title accessory need, not a single-game trend.
ideas.differentiation: Existing score dials found in the category are free-standing pucks or cards that sit loose on the table and get lost in the box; specifying a spring-jaw box-edge clip (rather than a flat base) as the mounting mechanism ties the accessory permanently to the game box itself, directly solving the 'lost accessory' problem that loose dials have.
ideas.producibility_notes: 2 parts: dial face (rotates on a central pin) and clip body (spring-jaw formed as two flexible arms molded into the single clip-body print, 1.5mm arm thickness for FDM flex durability). No glue; dial pin is a friction-fit post assembled by the user snapping the dial onto the clip body's center post once. No metal hardware.
ideas.margin_case: ~40g PLA, ~2.5hr print, sell at $12. Low material cost with a broad cross-game customer base (anyone who plays box-based tabletop games) supports strong margin at an impulse-buy price point typical of small board-game accessories.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A two-part rotating score-tracking dial that clips onto the edge of a board-game box lid. Part one is a circular dial face marked with a 0-50 number ring (two full rotations tracked via a small window showing 'x1'/'x2' as the dial completes a lap) that rotates freely around a central post. Part two is a clip body with two flexible spring-jaw arms shaped to grip over a box lid edge up to 12mm thick, with the dial's central post molded into its face. Purpose: A reusable, game-agnostic score-tracking accessory for board-game households, designed to stay clipped to the game box between sessions so it is never lost or left out of the box; sold as a small accessory/stocking-stuffer item for board-game hobbyists. Style: Minimal/utilitarian, clean number typography on the dial face, single or dual-color (dial face in one color, clip body in a contrasting color), no game-specific branding. Technical specification: Dial face 45mm diameter x 4mm thick with engraved/embossed numerals 0-50 in increments of 1 around the rim (numeral height minimum 2.5mm for legibility), a small pointer notch on the dial's edge, and a 6mm center through-hole. Clip body: a base plate 50mm x 20mm x 4mm with a 6mm diameter x 5mm tall center post (0.15mm clearance fit for the dial's through-hole, secured by a small friction-fit cap or press-over lip so the dial does not fall off but still rotates freely) and two spring-jaw arms extending from the base, each arm 35mm long x 8mm wide x 1.5mm thick, curved to grip a box edge up to 12mm thick with light spring pressure. Material: PLA or PETG (PETG preferred for the spring-jaw arms for flex durability), FDM, 2 printed parts, no metal hardware, single user assembly step of pressing the dial onto the post.

ideas.title: Shared-Table Two-Player Hands-Free Card Fan Tray
ideas.concept: A single tray molded with two mirrored hands-free card-fan racks side by side, separated by a raised opaque center divider tall enough to block each player's view of the other's fanned hand, for two players with limited hand strength or dexterity sharing one small table space.
ideas.rationale: Hands-free card holders for arthritis/limited-dexterity players are an established product category (multiple Amazon, Etsy, and 3D-print listings confirmed by search), and accessible-gaming advocacy within the hobby (e.g. accessibility-focused board-game review coverage) documents ongoing demand from assisted-living and multigenerational family game settings.
ideas.differentiation: Every existing hands-free card holder found in search is a single-user rack sold as an individual unit; none combine two racks into one shared tray with a built-in privacy divider, which is the specific configuration needed for two dexterity-limited players (e.g. at an assisted-living game table) to play a hidden-hand card game side by side without a third party having to hold cards for one of them.
ideas.producibility_notes: 1 part, single color, no assembly, no hardware. Fan slot grooves angled at 15 degrees, groove width 2mm to hold standard playing-card stock (0.3mm card thickness), divider wall height 60mm to reliably block sightlines. Print flat, base-down, no supports needed.
ideas.margin_case: ~95g PLA, ~5hr print, sell at $19. Accessible-gaming aids are typically bought by caregivers or facilities rather than price-sensitive individual gamers, supporting a higher per-unit price than a standard single-user card rack (which sell around $8-10).
ideas.prompt: Concept: A single tabletop tray containing two mirrored hands-free playing-card fan racks side by side, each rack made of a curved base with a row of angled slots that a standard deck of playing cards can be fanned into and stand upright without being held, separated down the middle by a tall opaque divider wall. Purpose: An accessibility card-game accessory for two players with limited hand strength or dexterity (e.g. arthritis, hand tremor, young children) to sit at the same small table space and each hold a private hand of cards hands-free, with the center divider preventing each player from seeing the other's cards; intended for home, senior-living, and multigenerational family use. Style: Minimal/utilitarian, smooth rounded edges for safe handling by users with limited grip strength, non-slip flat base texture, single neutral color (offer light wood-tone or off-white). Technical specification: Overall tray footprint 240mm wide x 90mm deep x 65mm tall at the divider's peak. Each of the two fan racks holds up to 15 standard playing cards (63mm x 88mm, ~0.3mm thick) in a curved slotted base 100mm wide x 60mm deep, with 15 slots per rack angled 15 degrees from vertical, each slot 2mm wide x 20mm deep, spaced 3mm apart center-to-center so fanned cards overlap legibly. Center divider wall: 10mm wide x 60mm tall x 90mm deep, positioned exactly between the two racks, opaque (solid infill, no through-gaps) to fully block sightlines between the two card fans when both players are seated. Base plate underside includes a shallow non-slip texture (ribbed pattern, 0.5mm ridge height) to resist sliding on a table. Material: PLA, FDM, single printed part, no supports required if printed base-down, no glue or hardware, no assembly.

ideas.title: Tool-Free Interlocking Modular Dungeon Tile Set
ideas.concept: A starter set of 12 square 3D dungeon-floor tiles (28mm-scale compatible) that connect edge-to-edge using a printed puzzle-piece lip and notch — no magnets, no pins, no separate connector pieces — so buyers can lay out or reconfigure a dungeon map by hand in seconds.
ideas.rationale: Modular 3D dungeon terrain (OpenForge-style systems and similar) is one of the most consistently active categories across Thingiverse/MyMiniFactory/Printables for the tabletop-RPG-adjacent board game crowd, reflecting sustained multi-year demand for reconfigurable terrain among D&D and dungeon-crawler board game players.
ideas.differentiation: Search confirms the dominant existing systems (OpenForge and its many remixes) rely on user-installed magnets or metal pins at every tile edge for connection, requiring the buyer to source and install dozens of small magnets themselves. This set is specified with a purely geometric press-fit lip-and-notch edge connector instead, so every tile in the set connects to every other tile straight out of the package with zero extra hardware or assembly labor.
ideas.producibility_notes: 12 tiles, single color (stone-gray), each roughly 50mm x 50mm x 8mm. Interlocking lip 2mm tall x 3mm deep on two adjacent edges, matching notch on the other two edges, printable flat with no supports. Batchable on one plate per set. No features under 1mm.
ideas.margin_case: ~280g PLA total for a 12-tile starter set, ~10hr print, sell at $32. Buyers avoid a multi-hour magnet-installation project (a known pain point in the existing hobby, per community threads) which justifies paying a premium over raw filament cost for a ready-to-connect set.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A 12-tile starter set of modular dungeon floor tiles, each a flat square slab with a stone-floor top surface, designed to connect edge-to-edge into a reconfigurable dungeon or room layout using only printed geometry — two adjacent edges of each tile have a raised interlocking lip, and the other two edges have a matching recessed notch, so tiles snap together by hand with a firm press-fit and no glue, magnets, or pins. Purpose: A modular terrain accessory for tabletop RPG and dungeon-crawler board game players (28mm miniature scale) who want to build and reconfigure floor layouts for games between sessions without installing hardware; sold as a starter expansion set for existing terrain collections or as a standalone basic dungeon kit. Style: Minimal/utilitarian stone-dungeon aesthetic — subtle flagstone surface texture on the top face, flat unadorned underside, single stone-gray color, no fine ornamental detail that would require supports. Technical specification: Each of the 12 tiles measures 50mm x 50mm (28mm-scale standard) x 8mm thick. Two adjacent edges of each tile carry a raised connector lip 2mm tall x 3mm wide running the full 50mm edge length; the opposite two edges carry a matching recessed notch 2.1mm tall x 3.1mm wide (0.1mm clearance for a firm friction press-fit that separates by hand when needed). Top surface has a shallow flagstone texture (groove depth 0.4mm) dividing it into an irregular 4-6 stone pattern per tile. All 12 tiles are geometrically identical (same lip/notch layout) so any tile connects to any other tile in any rotation. Material: PLA, FDM, single color, 12 separate flat parts printable together on one build plate with no supports needed (flat orientation, texture and lips face up), no glue, no magnets, no metal hardware, no assembly beyond hand-pressing tiles together.

ideas.title: Tuck Box Butler: Compact Filler-Game Deck Caddy
ideas.concept: A small tilted 3-compartment caddy (draw pile / discard pile / active hand) sized to fit inside the original small tuck box of compact filler card games, so players don't have to deal cards onto the bare table.
ideas.rationale: Small-box filler and trick-taking card games (the category including titles like Sea Salt & Paper, Sushi Go, and Love Letter) are a growth segment repeatedly highlighted in 2026 cozy/filler-game coverage, and unlike big-box euros these small games typically ship with zero insert at all, leaving a genuine unaddressed organizational gap rather than a saturated one.
ideas.differentiation: The organizer-insert category is dominated by big-box euro games (Ark Nova, Everdell, etc.) that already have dozens of free community inserts; small tuck-box filler games are comparatively underserved because their tiny boxes make injection-molded or free hobbyist inserts impractical to justify designing, which is exactly the gap this product targets with a deliberately compact, tilted 3-zone caddy sized to standard small tuck-box card dimensions (mini European size, ~44x68mm cards).
ideas.producibility_notes: 1 part, single color, no assembly. Tilted trays at 10 degrees for easy card pickup, wall thickness 1.5mm, external footprint sized to slide into a standard tuck box (approx 70mm x 95mm x 40mm box). No features under 1mm.
ideas.margin_case: ~30g PLA, ~2hr print, sell at $9. Small print volume keeps cost low; priced as an inexpensive impulse add-on next to the (typically $10-15) filler game itself, positioned as a natural bundle upsell rather than a standalone big-ticket purchase.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A single compact caddy insert with 3 tilted compartments (draw pile, discard pile, active hand/tableau) sized to fit inside the original small tuck box of a compact card game using mini European-size cards. Each compartment tilts backward at roughly 10 degrees so cards lean against the compartment wall and are easy to pick up with two fingers rather than lying flat on the table. Purpose: An in-box organizer accessory for small filler and trick-taking card games that ship with no insert at all, intended for board-game hobbyists who want faster setup and tidier play without needing a bigger box; sized to slide into and stay inside the game's original packaging. Style: Minimal/utilitarian, smooth rounded compartment edges, single neutral color (offer black, white, or natural), no game-specific branding or artwork. Technical specification: Overall external footprint 68mm wide x 92mm deep x 35mm tall, sized to slide into a standard small tuck box (approx 70mm x 95mm x 40mm interior). Three compartments arranged side by side: draw pile compartment 22mm wide x 70mm deep, discard pile compartment 22mm wide x 70mm deep, active hand/tableau compartment 24mm wide x 70mm deep, each tilted 10 degrees from vertical toward the front opening, wall thickness 1.5mm throughout, floor thickness 2mm. Card capacity per compartment: up to 55 mini-Euro cards (44mm x 68mm, ~0.3mm each) for draw/discard, fanned capacity of 10 cards for the tableau compartment. Material: PLA, FDM, single printed part, no supports required if printed compartment-openings-up, no glue or hardware, no assembly.

ideas.title: Adjustable-Arm Rotating Turn-Order Carousel
ideas.concept: A rotating disc marker with 6 fold-away arrow arms (fold flat or extend outward per player count 2-6) that sits in the center of the table and physically points to both the current player and, via a second shorter inner arrow, the next player up — rotated by hand each turn.
ideas.rationale: Turn-order/first-player marker upgrades are a long-running purchase category among board-game hobbyists (confirmed active listings across MakerWorld, Printables, Cults3D, and Etsy), showing durable cross-title demand for a physical turn-tracking object at the table, independent of any single game's theme.
ideas.differentiation: Every first-player marker found in search is a static single-purpose token (a coin, trophy, or figure indicating only whose turn it currently is) fixed to one player count. This design's fold-away multi-arm mechanism adjusts to table sizes of 2-6 players and adds a second, shorter inner arrow that simultaneously shows who goes next — a dual current/next-player indicator not present in any static token design found.
ideas.producibility_notes: 2 parts: base disc (with 6 hinged arm sockets molded in) and 6 identical fold-away arms attached via integrated print-in-place hinge pins (0.3mm clearance, snap-fit rotation joint). Single color. Arms fold flat against the disc when not needed for lower player counts.
ideas.margin_case: ~70g PLA, ~4hr print, sell at $16. A mechanical, adjustable turn-tracker is a novel gift item within an established accessory category, supporting a price above simple static first-player tokens (typically $6-10) due to the added functional mechanism.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A circular rotating turn-order marker for the center of a game table, consisting of a base disc with 6 identical arms attached at its rim via print-in-place hinges, each arm foldable flat against the disc or extended straight outward. One arm is marked as the 'current player' pointer (longer, bold arrowhead) and a second, shorter arrow is printed on the disc's top face pointing 60 degrees clockwise from the main arm to indicate 'next player'. Players fold out only as many arms as there are players (2 to 6), evenly spaced, position the disc so the main arm points at whoever's turn it is, and rotate the whole disc to the next folded-out arm position at the end of each turn. Purpose: A reusable, game-agnostic turn-order and first-player tracking accessory for board-game hobbyists who play a variety of multiplayer games and want a clearer, more functional turn indicator than a plain token; sold as a gift/accessory item. Style: Minimal/utilitarian geometric design, single bold color for high table visibility, clean arrow iconography, no game-specific branding. Technical specification: Base disc 60mm diameter x 6mm thick with a printed 'next player' arrow icon on its top face (arrowhead 8mm long) positioned 60 degrees offset from the primary arm's default position. 6 arm sockets evenly spaced around the disc rim, each socket housing a print-in-place hinge pin (4mm diameter x 6mm long, 0.3mm clearance) allowing its arm to rotate 90 degrees between flat-against-disc and fully-extended-outward positions with a small friction detent (0.5mm bump) holding each position. Each arm is 45mm long x 10mm wide x 3mm thick, tapering to a 6mm-wide arrowhead tip; one arm (marked with a distinct raised dot on its top face) is the 'current player' pointer. Material: PLA, FDM, printed as one build with print-in-place hinges (printed flat/disc-down, arms in the flat-against-disc position, so no supports are needed inside the hinge joints), single color, no glue or metal hardware, no post-print assembly beyond the first test-rotation of each arm.

ideas.title: Expandable Modular Sleeved-Card Library System
ideas.concept: A single deck-box module that holds up to 100 double-sleeved cards and connects side-by-side and stacks vertically with additional identical modules (sold and ordered separately over time) via a tab-and-groove edge lock, so a hobbyist's card-game shelf grows one module per new game rather than needing a new storage solution each time.
ideas.rationale: Sleeved-card deck storage (TCG/deck-builder boxes, 'bookshelf' style boxes) is a proven, high-volume purchase category confirmed across Etsy, MakerWorld, and MyMiniFactory listings, reflecting durable demand from the deck-building and living-card-game segment of board gamers who accumulate many decks over time.
ideas.differentiation: Search confirms existing bookshelf/vault-style deck boxes (e.g. 'Vault of Holding', 'Bookshelf Deck Box') are sold as fixed-capacity standalone units sized for a shelf or Kallax cube. This product is instead specified explicitly as a single expandable module with a standardized tab-and-groove edge connector on all 4 sides, so it is designed from the outset as the first purchase in an ongoing modular system a customer keeps buying into as their collection grows — a repeat-purchase product structure rather than a one-time storage box.
ideas.producibility_notes: 1 part per module (the unit sold), single color, snap-lid on the front face (press-fit, no hinge hardware). Tab-and-groove connectors (2mm tab, 2.1mm groove, 0.1mm clearance) on all 4 external edges so modules interlock in a grid in any direction. No features under 1mm.
ideas.margin_case: ~150g PLA per module, ~7hr print, sell at $17 per module. Because the connector system encourages buying multiple modules over time as the customer's game collection grows, expected customer lifetime purchases (3-6 modules per household) make this a strong repeat-revenue product despite a modest single-unit margin.
ideas.prompt: Concept: A single rectangular deck-storage module sized to hold up to 100 double-sleeved standard cards (66mm x 91mm sleeved) upright, with a front-facing snap-fit lid for access and a standardized tab-and-groove connector strip running along all 4 external edges so the module can interlock edge-to-edge and stack top-to-bottom with additional identical modules purchased separately, forming a growing modular 'library' shelf of card storage over time. Purpose: A deck-building and living-card-game storage accessory for board-game and card-game hobbyists who accumulate multiple decks across many games and want a storage system they can expand incrementally rather than replace; sold as the first unit in an ongoing modular system, marketed for repeat purchase as the buyer's collection grows. Style: Minimal/utilitarian, clean flat panel faces suitable for an optional label area on the spine, single neutral color per module (offer black, white, navy, and a small rotating set of accent colors for visual deck differentiation on a shelf), no game-specific branding. Technical specification: Module external dimensions 75mm wide x 105mm tall x 35mm deep, internal card cavity 70mm wide x 95mm tall x 30mm deep (holding approximately 100 double-sleeved cards standing on edge). Front face has a snap-fit lid: a flat panel 70mm x 100mm with a 2mm deep perimeter lip that press-fits into a matching perimeter groove on the module body (0.15mm clearance) and stays closed via friction, removable by hand without tools. All 4 external edges (top, bottom, left, right) carry a repeating tab-and-groove connector pattern: raised tabs 2mm tall x 2mm wide x 8mm long alternating with grooves 2.1mm deep x 2.1mm wide x 8mm long, spaced every 15mm along each edge, such that any module's edge can interlock with any other identical module's opposite edge in a firm press-fit requiring no glue or hardware. Material: PLA, FDM, single printed part (module body) plus one printed lid, 2 parts total per module, no supports required if module printed opening-up and lid printed flat, no glue or metal hardware, one snap-fit assembly step for the lid.
